dependency: Break the named operating dependency by excluding 70% vibration and forbidding escalation when flow drops. Use a predetermined 30% schedule and measure low doses instead of treating sustained strong vibration as necessary. The stipulated 30% comparison already challenges necessity: it retains discharge and gives larger doses in windows 2-4. This is comparative evidence within a synthetic trace, not proof that vibration-induced packing or any other mechanism caused the difference.

predictions.account: Hypothesis: accumulated vibration exposure produces a reversible local obstruction through packing or segregation; strong-vibration escalation could reinforce that obstruction.
predictions.result: Compared with the replicated 30% first-four-on reference, distributing the same 60 energized seconds as 12 seconds at 30% followed by 3 seconds off in every dispense window is predicted to reduce later low-dose errors or no-flow intervals if short releases interrupt obstruction. A separate reference-schedule trial with one measured 5 mm downward external mount tap after window 3 is predicted to recover some window-4 flow if obstruction is mechanically reversible. Neither recovery nor a visible band would identify packing fraction or composition.
predictions.when: Prospective four-trial allocation: trial 1 replicates the stipulated 30% first-four-on schedule; trial 2 changes only the predetermined drive schedule to 12 seconds on and 3 seconds off in each of five windows; trial 3 repeats the reference; trial 4 repeats the reference with the single specified tap during the 10-second off interval after window 3. Each uses a fresh 300 g charge, identical window boundaries and cup exchanges, fixed geometry and composition, and at most 60 energized seconds within 120 seconds. Compare individual errors, tolerance counts, cumulative mass, no-flow intervals and fill height; a duty-limit violation invalidates its trial.

predictions.account: Rival hypothesis: declining fill height and limited gravity discharge dominate the later dose decline, without an accumulating reversible obstruction.
predictions.result: The pulsed schedule is predicted to preserve a decline associated with fill height and may reduce early doses because each window receives less energized time. Energizing window 5 may improve its dose simply because the reference leaves that window off, so that improvement alone cannot establish obstruction release. The tap is predicted to produce no reproducible sustained recovery beyond reference variability if fill height is the dominant limitation.
predictions.when: Assess the same four trials, especially windows 2-4 and the recorded fill heights; separately report the changed energization of window 5. Different histories of discharged mass can produce different fill heights, so equal initial charge does not guarantee equal later head and the small trial budget limits discrimination.

predictions.account: Rival causal direction: pre-existing poor flow or batch-dependent resistance prompts the operator to increase vibration, rather than increased vibration initiating poor flow.
predictions.result: With escalation removed, this account predicts low-dose episodes can still arise under predetermined 30% drive and need not follow accumulated strong-vibration exposure. Fixed schedules prevent operator response from creating the proposed return link but cannot, by themselves, establish the reversed arrow. Replicate variability, unspecified moisture and unmeasured pressure leave this account viable even if a tap produces a transient recovery.
predictions.when: Record flow timing, switch timing and fill height throughout the prospective fixed-schedule trials. No new 70% escalation trial is introduced. Treat every proposed causal interpretation and future recovery as a hypothesis, and distinguish event ordering from established causation.

surviving_outcome: The valued outcome remains five successive 15-second doses of 25 +/- 2 g through the existing outlet, with fewer low-dose windows or a narrower spread as useful bounded partial results. After explicitly removing sustained 70% drive, the stipulated 30% comparison preserves two in-tolerance doses, 24 and 23 g, versus one, 26 g, under 70%; low-dose windows fall from four to three and the five-dose spread narrows from 22 to 19 g. Its doses of 21, 19 and 5 g still miss tolerance, so the full target has not survived as an achieved result. These are synthetic observed partial outcomes only; the proposed schedules and tap have no observed success. Any future partial benefit must declare its demonstrated fill range and retain enclosure, composition, geometry and duty constraints.
unknowns: Packing, segregation, moisture, drive coupling and other causes remain unresolved; pressure, packing fraction, actual band composition and calibrated acceleration are unavailable.
The pale band is visually described as fines-rich but its composition was not measured; visibility does not verify segregation or compaction.
No observation establishes five-window target feasibility across declining fill height within the energized-time limit.
Changing on-time distribution changes later fill history and the fifth-window drive state; a result cannot uniquely identify the hypothesized causal return path.
Four prospective trials provide limited repeatability evidence and no production, other-material, long-term or real-hardware performance claim.
